nodes.label: Emotional Feedback Loops
nodes.rationale: Functional feedback alone (green check, red X) is forgettable; pairing actions with encouragement, personality, and proportional celebration creates emotional reinforcement that drives retention.

nodes.label: Peak-End Rule
nodes.rationale: Nobel Prize-winning research by Daniel Kahneman shows the brain compresses an experience into two remembered moments, the peak and the end, so designing those two moments yields disproportionate perceived quality (Disney parks: 70% of visitors return for remembered moments, not a flawless day).

nodes.label: UI Lens vs UX Lens Separation
nodes.norm_label: ui lens vs ux lens separation
nodes.rationale: Gathering UI and UX inspiration separately prevents visual style from biasing structural decisions; visual direction is finalized before wireframing so stakeholder feedback stays about one dimension at a time.

nodes.label: 60/30/10 Color Rule
nodes.rationale: 60% neutral base, 30% complementary, 10% accent reserves strong color for meaningful moments (CTAs, key indicators); overusing accent color kills hierarchy.

nodes.label: Core Design Philosophy (Intentionality)
nodes.rationale: Great mobile UI is not about flashiness but intentionality: every pixel, spacing value, and color must serve the user and the primary goal, making interfaces feel smooth, personal, and alive rather than merely functional.

nodes.label: 8-Point Grid Spacing System
nodes.rationale: All spacing divisible by 8 or 4 plus relationship-based spacing (2x multiplier between groups) creates rhythm and encodes grouping without borders.

nodes.label: Thumb Zone
nodes.rationale: Primary actions belong in the bottom third of the screen because that is where thumbs comfortably reach, minimizing interaction cost on one-handed mobile use.

nodes.label: Typography Hierarchy Rule
nodes.rationale: Limiting to one font family, four sizes, and two weights (using size, weight, and opacity for hierarchy) prevents visual noise and keeps scanning effortless.

nodes.label: Audio Volume Limiter (60% Cap)
nodes.rationale: A software volume cap of 0.6 exists for baby hearing safety, so playback volume is clamped in the centralized audio layer rather than trusted to UI controls.
